s: Three Michelin stars inside a hotel tower in Chamartín, where chef Dabiz Muñoz treats each course as a small act of provocation.
w: Dabiz Muñoz built DiverXO into one of Europe's most theatrical tasting menus, fusing Asian, Mediterranean and Mexican technique into dishes staged with deliberately unsettling flourishes -- swinging props, painted tablecloths, scripted lines. It holds three Michelin stars and a permanent place near the top of the World's 50 Best list, in a dining room inside the NH Collection Eurobuilding hotel.

s: A stone asador on the square of a Basque hill hamlet, organised almost entirely around one idea: a wood fire adjusted by hand under everything that leaves the kitchen.
w: Bittor Arguinzoniz built his own charcoal and custom-height grills to cook nearly the whole menu over embers -- not just meat and fish, but butter, cheese and caviar smoked or seared to order. The restaurant occupies an old stone building on the square of Axpe, a hamlet at the foot of Mount Anboto. It was ranked No. 2 in The World's 50 Best Restaurants 2025 and named Best Restaurant in Europe.

s: A family-run grill on Getaria's harbourfront, refined over six decades into the reference point for whole grilled turbot on the Cantabrian coast.
w: Elkano opened as a modest quayside grill in 1964 and has spent decades perfecting one technique: whole fish, turbot above all, clamped in a hinged wire parrilla and cooked slowly over embers so the fat self-bastes the flesh. It sits a few streets from the fishing harbour in the town that also gave the world Juan Sebastián Elcano, the first captain to complete a circumnavigation.
_facts: Opened as a street-side grill in 1964

s: Albert Adrià's post-elBulli restaurant behind an unmarked door in Sant Antoni, run as a sequence of small rooms rather than one dining room.
w: After elBulli closed, Albert Adrià spent years developing Enigma as a single roughly 25-course experience spread across a cocktail bar, a raw bar and several kitchen counters, with no fixed table for the whole meal. The building was designed by RCR Arquitectes, the Pritzker Prize-winning Catalan studio, wrapped in a deliberately anonymous concrete-and-glass shell.
_facts: Chef Albert Adrià, formerly of elBulli

a: Calle de José Ortega y Gasset, Salamanca
s: An Italian dining room off Manuel Becerra where the wood-fired pizza has been ranked among Spain's best.
w: Baldoria serves Neapolitan-leaning pizza alongside a broader Italian menu, built around imported ingredients and a wood-fired oven, in Madrid's Salamanca district. It has placed in national best-pizza rankings and draws a steady local crowd near Manuel Becerra rather than trading mainly on tourist footfall.
_facts: Located in Salamanca/Lista neighbourhood near Manuel Becerra

s: A Gràcia pizzeria built around house-cured salumi and organic, seasonal toppings, ranked among the best pizzerias on earth.
w: What began as Garden Pizza in 2018 grew into Sartoria Panatieri, where Rafa Panatieri and Jorge Sastre apply haute-cuisine technique to Neapolitan-style dough and make much of their own charcuterie and cheese in house. In 2023 the 50 Top Pizza guide named it Best Pizzeria in Europe and third-best in the world.
_facts: Chefs Rafa Panatieri and Jorge Sastre
3rd Best Pizzeria in the World, Best in Europe, 50 Top Pizza 2023
Grew out of Garden Pizza, opened 2018

s: A gourmet pizzeria on Carrer de Balmes in Sant Gervasi, running a full seasonal Italian menu alongside its wood-fired pizzas.
w: La Balmesina operates as a complete Italian restaurant as much as a pizzeria, pairing a rotating seasonal menu with wood-fired pizza in the residential Sant Gervasi-Galvany stretch of Barcelona's uptown, building a steady neighbourhood following distinct from the city's more tourist-facing pizza scene.
_facts: Located on Carrer de Balmes, Sant Gervasi-Galvany
Combines full Italian menu with wood-fired pizza

s: A Neapolitan pizzeria in Chamberí, opened by two brothers who left marketing careers to bring 36-hour-fermented dough to Madrid.
w: Riccardo and Vittorio Figurato, two Neapolitan brothers, opened Fratelli Figurato in December 2017 after leaving corporate jobs, aiming to reproduce the pizza of Naples' old-school pizzerias. Their dough ferments at least 36 hours before firing in the plain brick-and-wood dining room on Calle Alonso Cano.
_facts: Opened December 2017 by brothers Riccardo and Vittorio Figurato

s: A four-storey house behind Plaza Mayor whose wood-fired oven has roasted suckling pig since 1725, earning Guinness's listing as the world's oldest restaurant.
w: Founded in 1725 by Jean Botín and his wife, Sobrino de Botín passed after their deaths to her nephew, giving it its enduring name. Guinness World Records recognises it as the oldest restaurant in continuous operation anywhere, and the same wood-burning oven from its founding still roasts the cochinillo and cordero that built its reputation, a few steps from Plaza Mayor.
_facts: Founded 1725; Guinness World Record for oldest restaurant
Original wood-fired oven still in use
Referenced in Hemingway's The Sun Also Rises

s: An all-you-can-eat dining hall on the edge of Narbonne, built around Auguste Escoffier's 19th-century recipes, with a cheese room alone stocking over a hundred varieties.
w: Les Grands Buffets serves a single-price buffet menu drawing on more than 150 recipes attributed to Auguste Escoffier, laid out across dedicated stations -- a seafood counter with a tiered lobster display, a charcuterie room, and a cheese platter holding a Guinness-recognised 111 varieties. It occupies a large hall inside the Espace de Liberté leisure complex at the edge of Narbonne.
_facts: Single-price all-you-can-eat format built on ~150 Escoffier recipes

s: A two-Michelin-star counter restaurant built around a raw produce display -- the ingredients are the décor.
w: Bruno Verjus, a former food writer with no formal culinary training, opened Table in 2013 near the Marché d'Aligre and built its reputation on radical ingredient-first cooking -- a whole turbot or a single Breton lobster presented before it's touched. Diners sit at a horseshoe counter around the open kitchen. It entered the World's 50 Best list at No. 8 in 2023 and holds two Michelin stars and a Green Star.
_facts: Two Michelin stars plus Green Star

s: A stripped-back workshop-loft dining room near Bastille that helped define Paris's bistronomy wave.
w: Chef Bertrand Grébaut trained under Alain Passard at Arpège before opening Septime in 2011 in a former workshop off Rue de Charonne -- bare wood tables, metal rafters, an open kitchen. The tasting menu shifts with the market almost daily, and a table here has been one of the hardest bookings in Paris for over a decade.
_facts: Trained at Arpège under Alain Passard

s: A three-Michelin-star temple to vegetables, near the Musée Rodin, where meat has been all but banished from the menu.
w: Alain Passard has held three Michelin stars at Arpège since 1996, and in the 2000s pivoted the entire kitchen toward his own kitchen gardens -- vegetables roasted, glazed, or turned into pastry, with animal protein now a footnote. The dining room, all pear wood and etched glass, remains one of the defining acts of modern French vegetable cookery.
_facts: Chef Alain Passard, three Michelin stars since 1996
Menu built around Passard's own vegetable gardens

s: A Neapolitan pizzeria on the Puteaux riverbank, a short walk from the Seine and the Île de Puteaux.
w: IMperfetto turns out Naples-style pizza -- long-fermented dough, blistered leopard-spotted crusts -- from a spot on Boulevard Richard Wallace just west of La Défense, drawing a mixed crowd of office workers and Puteaux residents rather than tourists.

s: A stone mountain refuge at 1,440 metres, at the treeline junction on Mont Ventoux's southern flank, where every cyclist stops.
w: Chalet Reynard sits at the point where the D974's forest switchbacks give way to the Giant of Provence's bare limestone summit cone -- one of the two roads up Ventoux and a fixture of Tour de France lore. It's served hikers, skiers and cyclists at this junction for decades, with truffle menus in season and simple omelettes and charcuterie the rest of the year.
_facts: Altitude ~1,440m, junction of the Bédoin and Sault ascents of Mont Ventoux
One of the oldest restaurants in Bédoin
Doubles as a small ski station in winter

q: Le Train Bleu Gare de Lyon Paris
s: A gilded 1900 Belle Époque dining room inside Gare de Lyon, painted ceilings and all, built for the World's Fair.
w: Opened in 1901 as the Buffet de la Gare de Lyon for the Exposition Universelle, Le Train Bleu is a listed historic monument -- forty-one painted ceiling panels depicting destinations once served by the PLM railway, gilt stucco, red velvet banquettes. It has featured in films from Nikita to Mr. Bean's Holiday.

s: A one-idea restaurant near Place Vendôme that has served nothing but soufflés, savory and sweet, since 1961.
w: Le Soufflé has built its entire menu -- starters, mains, desserts -- around a single technique for over sixty years, a stone's throw from Place Vendôme and the Tuileries. Cheese soufflé, lobster soufflé, Grand Marnier soufflé for dessert: the kitchen rises and falls on timing.

s: A gilded 18th-century dining room under the arcades of the Palais-Royal, dining since 1784 and freshly reborn in 2026.
w: Opened in 1784 as the Café de Chartres, renamed Le Grand Véfour in the 1820s, it sits under the Palais-Royal's arcaded galerie de Beaujolais -- sculpted wood panels, Louis XVI garlands, brass plaques marking where Napoleon and Colette once sat. After 34 years under Guy Martin, it reopened in late May 2026 under Paris Society with chef Bruno Doucet, its Historic Monument decor preserved.
_facts: Reopened May 2026 under chef Bruno Doucet

s: A tasting-menu room on the ground floor of a Brutalist Strand block, built around West African spice work and smoke.
w: Chef Jeremy Chan and Iré Hassan-Odukale moved Ikoyi from St James's Market to this raw-concrete Strand address in December 2022, pairing dishes like smoked jollof rice and plantain with a wine-and-sake-heavy list. It holds two Michelin stars and a place among the World's 50 Best Restaurants.
_facts: Co-founded by Jeremy Chan and Iré Hassan-Odukale

s: A Marylebone dining room where Mexican technique is rebuilt entirely from British and Nordic-trained instinct, with no lime or avocado in sight.
w: Santiago Lastra, formerly of Noma, opened Kol in October 2020 on Seymour Street, substituting British ingredients -- woodruff, sea buckthorn, kohlrabi -- for the produce a Mexican kitchen would normally reach for. It won a Michelin star in 2022 and has held it since.

s: A small Chiswick pizzeria that has been named Europe's single best pizzeria three years running, without ever leaving the neighbourhood parade it started on.
w: Michele opened Napoli on the Road on Devonshire Road in September 2019 after years selling pizza from a three-wheeled Piaggio Ape at markets. The Chiswick original has topped 50 Top Pizza's Europe ranking for 2024, 2025 and 2026, its dough long-fermented and toppings close to Neapolitan orthodoxy.
_facts: Ranked No.1 pizzeria in Europe, 50 Top Pizza, 2024-2026
Separate branches in Richmond and Soho

s: A third-generation Neapolitan pizzaiolo's London outpost on the traffic-heavy stretch between Trafalgar Square and Embankment.
w: Ciro Salvo, whose family has made pizza in Naples for three generations, opened this Northumberland Avenue branch of 50 Kalò in 2018 as his first venture outside Italy. His dough runs a 70% hydration and a long, slow ferment.

s: A Neapolitan pizzeria tucked under Chester's medieval Rows, run by an award-winning pizzaiolo far from the usual capital-city pizza circuit.
w: Stile Napoletano sits under the covered Rows on Watergate Street, inside Chester's Roman-grid old town, where chef Giacomo Guido bakes Neapolitan pizza to a standard that has drawn national food-press attention despite the setting being a provincial high street rather than Soho or Shoreditch.

s: A Mayfair dining room on the old Le Gavroche site, taken over by the chef who ran Restaurant Gordon Ramsay's kitchen for eight years running.
w: Matt Abé, who led Restaurant Gordon Ramsay to eight consecutive years of three Michelin stars, opened his first solo restaurant on Upper Brook Street in November 2025, on the site long occupied by Le Gavroche. Three months later, in the Michelin Guide UK 2026, Bonheur was awarded two stars outright.
_facts: Opened November 2025, chef Matt Abé (ex-Restaurant Gordon Ramsay)

q: Reale Niko Romito Castel di Sangro
s: A three-Michelin-star kitchen inside a restored 16th-century monastery in the Abruzzo mountains, run by Niko Romito.
w: Reale occupies Casadonna, a former monastery the Romito family rebuilt into a hotel, cooking school and dining room around five-century-old stone stable troughs, now part of a cellar holding over 5,000 bottles. Niko Romito built it to three Michelin stars by 2014 on a technique of stripped-back, ingredient-first Abruzzese cooking.
_facts: Restaurant relocated to the Casadonna estate in 2001
Estate vineyard grows Pecorino grapes at 860m

s: The Alajmo family's three-Michelin-star flagship in a nondescript stretch of Sarmeola di Rubano, west of Padua.
w: Le Calandre sits on an unassuming suburban road outside Padua, giving no hint of what's inside: Massimiliano Alajmo took it to three Michelin stars in 2003 at age 28, the youngest chef in the world to do so at the time. The kitchen's guiding idea -- lightness and clarity of flavour -- still shapes the menu run with his brother Raffaele.
_facts: Located in Sarmeola, a frazione of Rubano

s: Enrico Crippa's three-Michelin-star dining room on Alba's central square, in the heart of the Langhe truffle country.
w: Set right on Alba's main piazza, this is Enrico Crippa's stage for turning the Langhe's produce -- much of it from the restaurant's own kitchen garden -- into precise, vegetable-forward tasting menus. Alba is the epicentre of the white truffle trade every autumn.
_facts: Chef Enrico Crippa trained under Gualtiero Marchesi

s: Mauro Uliassi's three-Michelin-star seafood restaurant, built right onto the harbour channel of this Adriatic beach town.
w: Uliassi sits on the working harbour of Senigallia, close enough to the water that the dining room looks straight over the channel and the beach beyond. Mauro Uliassi has run it since the late 1980s, building a reputation on Adriatic seafood cooked with technical precision, and took it to three Michelin stars in 2019.
_facts: Chef Mauro Uliassi has run it since the 1980s

s: Norbert Niederkofler's three-Michelin-star 'Cook the Mountain' restaurant inside a repurposed 19th-century textile-mill villa in the Dolomites.
w: The restaurant relocated in 2023 into a 19th-century villa that once belonged to the Moessmer wool-mill estate. Niederkofler's 'Cook the Mountain' philosophy uses only hyper-local South Tyrolean ingredients -- no lemons, no olive oil, no imports -- across a twelve-course tasting menu.
_facts: Three Michelin stars plus Green Star
Relocated to the Moessmer villa estate in 2023
